div.head: Ine 54
div.ab: XCVIII. Se þe bið werfæhðe betogen ⁊ he onsacan wille þæs sleges mid aðe, þonne sceal bion on þære hyndenne an kyningæde be XXX hida, swa be gesiðcundum men swa be cierliscum, swa hwæþer swa hit sie.
XCVIII. Se þe bið werfæhðe betogen ⁊ he onsacan wille þæs sleges mid aþe, þonne sceal beon on þære hyndenne an cyningæðe be XXX hida, swa be gesiðcundum men swa be cierliscum, swa hwæðer swa hit sy.

Be werfæhðe tyhlan. Se ðe bið werfæhðe betogen ⁊ he ætsacan wylle ðæs slæges mid aðe, ðonne sceal beon on ðære hyndene an cyningæðe be ðrittig hída, swa be gesiþcundum men swa be ceorliscum, swa hweðer swa hít sy.

Qui þerfehþe (id est de homicidio) fuerit accusatus et negare uoluerit occisionem illius cum iureiurando, tunc debet esse in ea societate unum regium iusiurandum per triginta hidas, sic de siþcundo homine, sic de cirlisco.

[Be werfæhðe tyhlan.] Se þe bið werfæhðe betogen ⁊ he onsacan wille þæs sleges mid aðe, þonne sceal bion on þære hyndenne an kyningæðe be XXX hida, swa be gesiðcundum men swa be cierliscum, swa hwæþer swa hit sie.

{XCVIII} Se þe bið werfæhðe betogen ⁊ he onsacan wille þæs sleges mid aðe, þonne sceal bion on þære hyndenne an kyningæde be XXX hida, swa be gesiðcundum men swa be cierliscum, swa hwæþer swa hit sie.

[Wenn] einer der Menschen-Erschlagung beschuldigt wird und er von diesem Todtschlage sich durch Eid rein schwören will, dann soll in [je]der Hundertzahl [der Eideshiden] ein Königs-Eideshelfer [im Eideswerth] von 30 Hiden sein, sowohl bei einem [erschlagenen] Manne vom Gefolgsadel, wie bei einem gemeinfreien, wie immer es sei.

[If] someone is accused of homicide and he wishes to clear himself of this killing by oath, then in [each] hundred [of the oath-hides] there is to be one king’s oath-helper [of an oath-value] of 30 hides, whether for a [slain] man of the retainer nobility or for a common freeman, whichever it may be.

If anyone is accused of homicide and he wishes to deny the deed with an oath, there shall be in the 100 hides one entitled to give a king's oath of 30 hides, both in the case of the noble and the commoner—whichever he may be.

He who is accused of homicide, and wishes to deny the slaying with an oath—then there shall be in the hundred [hides] a man entitled to swear a king’s oath at 30 hides, both in the case of a gesith-born man or a ceorl, whichever it be.

He who is accused of an act of violence requiring payment of wergild, and he wishes to deny the slaying under oath, then there shall be in the hundred one [who can swear] the king’s oath [to the value of] thirty hides, both in the case of a nobly born man and for a man of ceorl rank, whichever it be.

note.seg: hund hatte ursprünglich Dekade bedeutet; daher denkt Price hier irrig an eine Schar von 10 und vergleicht tourbe von 10 témoins des Französ. MA.; Kemble (Saxons I 244) versteht ein Dorf von 10 Haushalten. Earle (Landchar. l) nimmt diese Bed. sogar für twelf(syx)-hynde an: Anführer von 120 (60) Mann. S. dagegen Sievers Gramm. § 95; Cosijn Altwestsä. Gr. § 48; Sweet Phonology 327. — Vgl. Eideshelfer 16. 18. a; Eideshufen 7a. Die Richtigkeit des Eides soll gewährleistet werden dadurch, dass ihn nicht bloss Bauern, sondern, wenn Erschlagener gemeinfrei (sechs-, oder 12 hynde) war, wenigstens zwei (6, bzw. 12) Männer von besonderer Beziehung zum Könige mitschwören. Zur Teilnahme höher Gestellter bei der Eideshilfe vgl. Alvred Beverlac. (c. 1150): Si accusator super accusatum 6. manu iuraverit, et unus de illis 6 dapifer domini sui fuerit, tunc accusatus iuramento 18 se purgabit, et unus illorum 18 erit dapifer S. Johannis, des Doms; Libert. eccl. S. Joh. Beverlac. bei Raine Sanctuar. Dunelm. (Surtees soc. 1837) 103; vgl. Beispiel aus Schottland, 13. Jh., bei Palgrave Rise 217

hund had originally meant a decade; hence Price wrongly thinks here of a band of 10 and compares the tourbe of 10 témoins of the French Middle Ages; Kemble (Saxons I 244) understands a village of 10 households. Earle (Landchar. l) even assumes this meaning for twelf(syx)-hynde: leader of 120 (60) men. See, against this, Sievers Gramm. § 95; Cosijn Altwestsä. Gr. § 48; Sweet Phonology 327. — Cf. Eideshelfer 16. 18. a; Eideshufen 7a. The correctness of the oath is to be guaranteed by its being sworn not merely by peasants but, if the slain man was a common freeman (six-, or 12 hynde), also by at least two (6, or 12, respectively) men with a special relationship to the king. On the participation of men of higher standing in oath-helping cf. Alvred Beverlac. (c. 1150): Si accusator super accusatum 6. manu iuraverit, et unus de illis 6 dapifer domini sui fuerit, tunc accusatus iuramento 18 se purgabit, et unus illorum 18 erit dapifer S. Johannis, of the minster; Libert. eccl. S. Joh. Beverlac. in Raine Sanctuar. Dunelm. (Surtees soc. 1837) 103; cf. an example from Scotland, 13th cent., in Palgrave Rise 217

Vgl. Wb: æwda, wo postvokalisch w geschwunden, wie bei Ælfred in æw, awðer; Cosijn Altwests. Gr. S. 197. Daneben hält Toller s. v. cyningæðe: ‘king’s oath’ nach Q mit Price-Thorpe für möglich. — Der cyninges geneat schwört nach Ine 19, wenn nicht huslgenga, ebenfalls für 30 Hufen, also sechsmal so wertvoll wie der Gemeinfreie, er hat wohl 1200 Schill. Wergeld wie Königsthegn. — Brunner II 386 hält ihn durch den königlichen Beamten aus der schwörenden Magschaft erwählt

Cf. Wb: æwda, where postvocalic w has been lost, as in Ælfred in æw, awðer; Cosijn Altwests. Gr. p. 197. Besides this, Toller, s. v. cyningæðe: also considers ‘king’s oath’ possible, following Q, with Price-Thorpe. — According to Ine 19 the cyninges geneat, if not a huslgenga, likewise swears for 30 hides, and is thus six times as valuable as the common freeman; he probably has a wergild of 1200 shill., like the king’s thegn. — Brunner II 386 holds that he was chosen from the swearing kindred by the royal official
Nicht ‘120’, wie Price empfiehlt, meinend, der Königsthegn schwöre für 120 Hufen
Not ‘120’, as Price recommends, supposing that the king’s thegn swore for 120 hides
Es kann nicht beklagter Totschläger gemeint sein; denn in diesem Falle galt ja des Hauptschwörers Eid, wenn adlig, selbst schon 30 Hufen
The accused slayer cannot be meant; for in that case the oath of the principal swearer, if he was noble, was in itself already worth 30 hides
i.e. in each 100 hides required in the oath (cf. note, cap. 14).

The expression kyningæde is obscure, but 30 hides was probably the value of the oath of a twelfhynde man (cf. cap. 19 above) If this is correct, it would mean that each 100 hides of the oath required must contain the oath of a twelfhynde man (see Liebermann’s note ad loc. and Chadwick, Anglo-Saxon Institutions, p. 148). ‘Whichever he may be,’ refers most probably to the man slain, but this is not absolutely certain.

note.label: [hides]
note.seg: e.g. if an oath, expressed in hides, was to be given in a suit where the fine involved was a freeman’s wergild of 200 shillings, there would have to be two men entitled to swear for 30 hides; if the highest wergild were involved, of 1200 shillings, there would have to be twelve of them.
